content: For a small single-table SQLite store, stdlib sqlite3 is simpler, has zero extra dependency weight, and keeps SQL explicit (fits a hand-rolled repository behind a Protocol interface, per Clean Architecture). SQLAlchemy earns its cost at multi-table/relational scale needing migrations across engines. sqlite-utils (Simon Willison) is a productivity layer over sqlite3 (schema-on-insert convenience) but adds an abstraction that obscures the explicit SQL a reviewer/interviewer would want to see in a from-scratch hackathon repo.
